PGS000327 is the better-supported ASD PRS because its endpoint fidelity is clean: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to “Autism spectrum disorder,” whereas PGS002790 has an explicit phenotype mismatch (phenotyping_reported = “Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)”) despite the ASD label fields. PGS000327 also comes from a disease-focused ASD GWAS meta-analysis context (Nat Genet ASD variants paper) with clear multi-cohort development and provides a meaningful effect size (OR=1.33) plus higher reported variance explained (R²=0.0245) than PGS002790’s small partial R² (~0.0055) from a broader sex-specific psychiatric/cognition study with unknown training sample size. Both are EUR-only and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R², so the decisive factors are phenotype alignment and stronger, more coherent disease-focused evidence in PGS000327.

Both candidates are near-clones: identical trait/phenotyping (basal cell carcinoma), same publication, same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL ancestry, same training (n=11,734) and validation size (n=11,322), and same basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2; both only show full-model AUROC=0.632, which cannot strongly differentiate PRS quality. As a tie-break within this matched context, PGS000454 has slightly stronger reported performance signals (Nagelkerke R² 0.0489 vs 0.0487; OR top 1% vs rest 3.79 vs 3.61) with essentially identical per-SD OR, so it edges PGS000452, but the advantage is marginal hence low confidence.

Both candidates target the same combined endpoint (trait_efo includes atrial flutter; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported are atrial fibrillation and flutter), but PGS001339 provides cleaner PRS-comparable performance evidence: explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.613 and PGS-only R2=0.02447 (no covariates), which also stays well below the atrial flutter heritability ceiling noted in the context. PGS001841 reports only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.1026) and no PRS-only AUC/R2, making its predictive strength harder to compare directly. Covariates are similarly basic in both (age/sex/PCs/array-type style), and both are UKB-derived framework-style scores with multi-ancestry evaluation, so the decisive advantage is PGS001339’s explicit PRS-only metrics versus PGS001841’s weaker/less standard metric reporting.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all basal cell carcinoma), study family (Cancer PRSweb), ancestry (EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL), covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), and training/validation sizes (n=11,734 train; n=11,322 eval). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we rely on within-family empirical performance signals: PGS000454 shows consistently stronger discrimination/effect evidence than PGS000447 (full-model AUROC 0.632 vs 0.591; Nagelkerke R² 0.0489 vs 0.0237; OR per SD 1.661 vs 1.398; top 1% vs rest OR 3.79 vs 2.5). Variant count differences (27 vs 72) are secondary here and do not outweigh the materially stronger observed performance/effect sizes for PGS000454 under otherwise identical design.

Both candidates are near-clones: same trait/phenotyping (basal cell carcinoma), same EFO, same method (P+T), same EUR-only training/evaluation, same training cohort (MGI), same covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), and same validation sample size (n=11,322), with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported for either (only full-model metrics). With endpoints and design effectively identical, the small full-model AUROC/R2 differences are minor, but PGS000454 is slightly stronger on the visible discrimination metrics (full-model AUROC 0.632 vs 0.628; Nagelkerke R² 0.0489 vs 0.0457) and has a slightly higher per-SD OR (1.661 vs 1.634) and more variants (27 vs 23). PGS000458’s only notable edge is a marginally higher top-1% vs rest OR (4.03 vs 3.79), which is not enough to outweigh the otherwise slightly stronger overall metric/structure profile of PGS000454.

PGS002786 is the better match to the target trait (bipolar disorder): its trait_reported/trait_efo are exactly bipolar disorder, whereas PGS002788 targets the narrower subtype bipolar II disorder (type 2). Both candidates come from the same publication, use the same method (SDPR), have similar genome-wide variant counts, identical EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, identical basic covariates (age, PCs1-3), and the same validation sample size (n=2,524), so study design/transportability do not differentiate them. The slightly higher reported partial R² for PGS002788 (0.00307 vs 0.00251) is a small full-model/partial metric difference on different non-disease phenotypes and is not enough to outweigh the endpoint-fidelity advantage of the exact bipolar disorder model.

Both candidates are near-clones: identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (basal cell carcinoma), same publication, same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL ancestry, same training cohort (MGI) and training/validation sample sizes, and both lack PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model metrics with basic covariates). With endpoint fidelity and study context indistinguishable, the only differentiators are marginal performance/effect-size differences: PGS000458 has slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.628 vs 0.63 is essentially tied but selected record shows 0.628 vs 0.63), slightly higher Nagelkerke R² (0.0457 vs 0.0456), and slightly higher top-1% OR (4.03 vs 3.95) with essentially identical per-SD OR. Given these tiny gaps and non-PRS-only metrics, the edge for PGS000458 is minimal, hence low confidence.

Both candidates are near-clones: same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (basal cell carcinoma), same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL ancestry, same training cohort (MGI) and training N (11,734), same covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), and same validation N (11,322). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2; only full-model AUROC/R2 are available and are very close. PGS000452 has slightly better full-model discrimination (AUROC 0.632 vs 0.628; Nagelkerke R² 0.0487 vs 0.0457) and slightly higher per-SD OR (1.663 vs 1.634), while PGS000458 only leads on top-1% vs rest OR (4.03 vs 3.61). Given the otherwise indistinguishable design and the small metric differences, PGS000452 edges out on the more general full-model AUROC/R² and per-SD effect size, but confidence is low due to the near-tie and lack of PRS-only metrics.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity and study context: identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported ("Disorders of bilirubin excretion" mapped to bilirubin metabolism disease), same UKB-only development (n=391,124), same covariates (age/sex/PCs etc.; no leakage signals), same ancestry distribution and validation size (n=19,924), and essentially identical PRS-comparable performance evidence (partial-r=0.0716 with overlapping CIs; no PRS-only AUC/R2 for either). With metrics and phenotype alignment unable to differentiate, the structural tie-break favors PGS002032 because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far broader variant coverage (19,768 vs 22 for PGS001824), which is generally more likely to capture polygenic signal than an extremely sparse penalized-regression score in this framework setting.

Both candidates are from the same publication (Cancer PRSweb), same endpoint fields (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all basal cell carcinoma), same ancestry context (EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL), same training cohort (MGI) and training/validation sizes, and both lack PRS-only AUC/R2 (so full-model AUROC is only a within-family signal). Given otherwise near-identical design and covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), PGS000452 shows consistently stronger reported performance/effect evidence than PGS000447: higher full-model AUROC (0.632 vs 0.591), higher pseudo-R² (0.0487 vs 0.0237), higher OR per SD (1.663 vs 1.398), and higher top-1% vs rest OR (3.61 vs 2.5). With no PRS-only metrics to favor the P+T construction in PGS000447, the stronger empirical discrimination signals make PGS000452 better supported.

Both candidates are near-clones: same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (basal cell carcinoma), same publication, same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL ancestry, same training cohort (MGI) and training/validation sample sizes, same basic covariates, and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model metrics, which are not decisive). With endpoints and context effectively identical, the small full-model AUROC/R2 differences are negligible; the best differentiator is the per-SD effect size, where PGS000454 has a slightly higher OR (1.661 vs 1.633) and β (0.507 vs 0.49) than PGS000456, supporting marginally stronger PRS signal. Confidence is low because differences are very small and both rely on non-PRS-only metrics.

Both candidates are from the same publication (Cancer PRSweb), same endpoint fields (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all basal cell carcinoma), same EUR-only ancestry context, same training cohort (MGI), same training n (11,734), same covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), and same validation size (11,322), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (so full-model AUROC is only a within-family signal). Given this near-clone setup, PGS000456 shows consistently stronger reported performance/effect evidence than PGS000447: higher full-model AUROC (0.63 vs 0.591), higher pseudo-R² (0.0456 vs 0.0237), higher top-1% OR (3.95 vs 2.5), and higher per-SD OR (1.633 vs 1.398). PGS000447 has more variants (72 vs 30) and a P+T method label, but within this same-study/same-endpoint comparison the empirical discrimination/effect-size advantage of PGS000456 is the more direct support.

Both candidates are near-clones from the same publication (Transl Psychiatry), same method (SDPR), similar genome-wide variant counts (~936k), same EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, same basic covariates (age, PCs1-3), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R² (only small partial R² values). Endpoint fidelity to the target trait (bipolar disorder) is comparable: PGS002788 targets bipolar II and PGS002787 targets bipolar I, both subtypes of bipolar disorder. With no clean PRS-only metrics to separate them, the only differentiator is the selected partial R², where PGS002788 is slightly higher (0.00307 vs 0.00275), so it narrowly wins; however the difference is tiny and phenotyping_reported differs (sluggish cognitive tempo vs DSM5 depression), making this a low-confidence choice.

Both candidates are near-clones: same target endpoint fields (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all basal cell carcinoma), same method family (P+T), same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL ancestry, same training cohort (MGI) and training/validation sample sizes, and similarly light covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported for either (so full-model AUROC is only a secondary within-family signal). Given this like-for-like context, PGS000458 has consistently stronger reported validation evidence than PGS000447: higher full-model AUROC (0.628 vs 0.591), higher pseudo-R² (0.0457 vs 0.0237), stronger top-1% vs rest OR (4.03 vs 2.5), and stronger per-SD OR (1.634 vs 1.398). The higher variant count in PGS000447 (72 vs 23) does not outweigh the materially better observed discrimination/effect-size signals in PGS000458 within the same study and endpoint.

PGS001824 is the better-supported match to the target bilirubin metabolism disease on endpoint fidelity: it is specifically for “Disorders of bilirubin excretion” with trait_efo exactly “bilirubin metabolism disease,” whereas PGS000924 targets a broader combined endpoint (“Disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism”) and is explicitly time-to-event, adding phenotype/endpoint mismatch risk for a generic disease target. Although PGS000924 reports clean PRS-only AUROC/R², its PRS-only R²=0.218 is implausibly above the provided local heritability ceiling (h2_obs≈0.089), making the metric suspect/non-comparable; PGS001824 avoids this issue (no PRS-only AUC/R² reported) and provides a modest partial correlation estimate. Both are UKB-derived framework-style scores with basic covariates and multi-ancestry evaluation, so the decision is driven mainly by tighter phenotype alignment and the heritability sanity-check concern against PGS000924.

Both candidates map to the correct concept (trait_efo includes atrial flutter), but PGS002050 has a more endpoint-faithful generic diagnosis phenotype (“Atrial fibrillation and flutter”) whereas PGS001339 is explicitly time-to-event (TTE), which is a mild mismatch for a generic atrial flutter target. PGS001339 does provide clean PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.613; R2=0.0245) that are plausible vs the heritability ceiling, but it comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“across 813 traits”, snpnet, only 2,142 variants), which domain guidance flags as systematically less reliable for external performance than genome-wide shrinkage-style scores. PGS002050, despite lacking PRS-only AUC/R2, uses LDpred2 with genome-wide coverage (~555k variants) and is evaluated across multiple ancestries, giving it the stronger overall evidence package for a standalone PRS for this endpoint.

PGS002032 is the better-supported choice for the target trait (bilirubin metabolism disease) because its endpoint is a direct match: trait_reported/phenotyping_reported are both “Disorders of bilirubin excretion” mapped solely to the target EFO. Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity and study context: same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (corneal dystrophy), same UKB portability publication, same training cohort/size (UKB; n=391,124), same covariates (age/sex/PCs etc.), same ancestry distribution and validation sample size (n=19,321), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2. With metrics largely non-discriminating, PGS002042 has the stronger available PRS-comparable evidence (higher partial correlation 0.0471 vs 0.0384 for PGS001835) and a structurally stronger genome-wide shrinkage approach with far broader variant coverage (LDpred2; 59,944 variants vs penalized regression sparse 38 variants), which is a meaningful tie-break within the same framework family.

Both candidates are from the same Nat Med paper, use the same method (LDpred2), have identical trait/phenotyping alignment to coronary artery disease, similar training N (116,649), identical basic covariates (age, sex, 10 PCs), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2—so performance must be judged mainly by effect size and structural/transportability signals. PGS003726 has a stronger reported PRS effect (HR 1.73 vs 1.67 for PGS003727) and a modestly larger variant count (1,296,172 vs 1,125,113), both supportive within the same method family. It also shows broader multi-cohort development (BBJ, FinnGen, MVP, etc.) than PGS003727 (CARDIoGRAMplusC4D, UKB only), which is mildly supportive for transportability. PGS003727’s slightly more diverse evaluation ancestry mix and higher record_count are weak differentiators and don’t outweigh the stronger HR and broader development context of PGS003726.

PGS000726 is better supported for the generic target trait “cirrhosis of liver” because its phenotyping_reported is a direct cirrhosis endpoint (“Cirrhosis”) with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs) and it comes from a large, multi-cohort cirrhosis-focused study (multiple biobanks; training n=346,840) with multi-ancestry evaluation. It also provides PRS-relevant effect-size evidence (OR per SD 1.32; OR top vs bottom quintile 2.26). In contrast, PGS000776 is more subtype/setting-specific (GWAS for alcohol-related cirrhosis, while its phenotyping_reported references incident cirrhosis in an NAFLD at-risk cohort with time-to-first hospitalization), making endpoint fidelity to generic cirrhosis less clean, and its only discrimination metric is a full-model C-index/AUC=0.677 (not PRS-only), with much smaller training (n=4,613) and single-cohort development (UKB).

Both candidates are near-clones for CAD (same trait_reported/efo/phenotyping_reported, same LDpred2 method, same variant count, same training n and validation n, and similarly clean basic covariates). With no PRS-only AUC/R2 for either, the main differentiators are effect-size evidence and study/transportability metadata. PGS003725 reports stronger discrimination evidence (includes both HR=1.75 and OR=2.14 per SD, both strong, vs PGS003726 only HR=1.73) and shows broader multi-ancestry evaluation coverage plus a richer multi-cohort development list, whereas PGS003726 has fewer supporting performance records and less effect-size reporting. Differences are modest, so confidence is Moderate.

PGS000704 is better supported despite being for the alcoholic subtype: its phenotyping_reported and trait_efo are coherent with cirrhosis (alcoholic liver cirrhosis), and it has a much stronger structural evidence package (snpnet multi-PRS with 183,271 variants vs 9 GWAS-hit variants in PGS000776) plus an explicit PRS effect size (HR 1.18 per SD). Both candidates lack PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model C-index values (0.711 for PGS000704 vs 0.677 for PGS000776) are only weakly informative; however, PGS000704’s covariate set remains basic (age/sex/PCs/batch) and its evaluation ancestry is reported (EUR/MAE), whereas PGS000776 has a notable endpoint mismatch in phenotyping_reported (incident cirrhosis in NAFLD at-risk individuals, time-to-first hospitalization) and evaluation ancestry is not reported. Overall, PGS000704 has cleaner endpoint coherence for cirrhosis-as-disease and stronger model construction evidence than PGS000776’s sparse, context-restricted score.

PGS003727 is better supported for the target CAD endpoint because it matches the generic disease phenotype cleanly (phenotyping_reported: “Coronary artery disease” vs PGS000018 explicitly “prevalent”), uses only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), and comes from a clearly disease-focused, modern multi-ancestry CAD PRS study with large evaluation (n=308,264) and explicit multi-ancestry EVAL distribution. Both candidates lack PRS-only AUC/R2, so PGS000018’s reported AUROC=0.89 is a full-model metric and not comparable PRS evidence; with similar per-SD effect size strength (PGS003727 HR=1.67 vs PGS000018 OR=1.6), the cleaner endpoint framing and broader external evaluation context favor PGS003727 despite PGS000018’s metaGRS/variant count and many cohorts.

Both candidates match the target CAD endpoint cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all coronary artery disease) and neither provides PRS-only AUC/R2, so we rely on study archetype/transportability and effect-size evidence. PGS003726 comes from a CAD-focused multi-ancestry PRS paper (Nat Med) with explicitly multi-ancestry evaluation split evenly across AFR/EAS/EUR/SAS and shows a stronger per-SD effect size (HR=1.73) than PGS002244’s OR=1.64, both in the “strong” range. PGS002244 has more variants and slightly larger training/validation N, but it is from a broad ‘common diseases across ancestries’ framework-style paper and its extra scale/variant count doesn’t compensate given similar covariates and no cleaner PRS-only metrics. Hence PGS003726 is better-supported overall.

PGS004913 is better supported for the target because its endpoint is tightly aligned to cirrhosis as a disease entity (alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis; EFO alcoholic liver cirrhosis) and its phenotyping_reported matches that diagnosis directly, whereas PGS000776’s phenotyping_reported is a more mismatched at-risk NAFLD time-to-event hospitalization endpoint (incident cirrhosis in NAFLD-risk individuals), which is a weaker fit for generic “cirrhosis of liver.” Neither candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so PGS000776’s full-model C-index=0.677 is not a comparable PRS metric; in contrast PGS004913 provides PRS-relevant effect evidence (OR top vs bottom deciles 4.4) and an R²=0.029 (not labeled PRS-only but at least a direct variance-explained signal) with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs). Overall, stronger phenotype fidelity plus more directly PRS-informative effect evidence favors PGS004913 despite PGS000776’s larger validation sample.

Both candidates are endpoint-faithful to coronary artery disease (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match) and neither provides PRS-comparable AUC/R2, so the decision rests on study archetype/transportability and effect-size evidence. PGS003727 comes from a CAD-focused Nat Med paper explicitly about a multi-ancestry CAD PRS and shows broad multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/EAS/EUR/MAE/SAS) with a strong per-SD effect size (HR=1.67). PGS002244 is from a broad cross-disease framework-style paper (“common diseases across ancestries”) and, while it has larger variant count and slightly larger training/validation N, its evidence is less disease-focused and its per-SD effect size is slightly weaker (OR=1.64). With metrics otherwise missing, the disease-focused multi-ancestry CAD study context and slightly stronger effect size favor PGS003727.

PGS003726 is better supported for the target CAD endpoint because it has cleaner endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported is simply “Coronary artery disease” vs PGS000018 explicitly “Coronary artery disease (prevalent)”), a much stronger and more directly PRS-informative effect size (HR per SD 1.73 vs OR 1.6), and a substantially broader, explicitly multi-ancestry evaluation design (AFR/EAS/EUR/SAS each 25%) with large validation (n=308,264). PGS000018’s main apparent performance signal is AUROC=0.89, but it is a full-model metric (not PGS-only) and therefore not comparable as PRS evidence; additionally its training sample is small (n=3,000) despite many listed cohorts. With both candidates lacking PRS-only AUC/R2, the stronger effect-size evidence plus broader evaluation context favors PGS003726.

PGS000726 is the better-supported match to the target trait (cirrhosis of liver): its trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are generic “Cirrhosis/cirrhosis of liver,” aligning directly with the umbrella endpoint, whereas PGS004913 is explicitly restricted to the subtype “Alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis” (trait_efo: alcoholic liver cirrhosis), which is a narrower, population/exposure-conditioned endpoint. Despite both lacking clean PRS-only AUC/R², PGS000726 has stronger study support and transportability signals: much larger multi-cohort development (ACG, ARIC, BBJ, BioVU, FinnGen, UKB, etc.) and multi-ancestry evaluation (EUR/AFR/NR) with a substantially larger validation sample (n=30,469) versus PGS004913’s EUR-only setting and smaller training/validation (n=3,037 / n=3,360). PGS004913 reports an R²=0.029 and OR top vs bottom deciles=4.4, but the R² appears to be full-model (not PRS-only) and the endpoint restriction to heavy drinkers/alcohol-associated cirrhosis limits generalizability to overall cirrhosis risk compared with PGS000726’s broader cirrhosis endpoint and comparable basic covariates.

PGS002244 is better supported for standalone CAD PRS selection because it has clean endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported exactly “Coronary artery disease” vs PGS000018’s “Coronary artery disease (prevalent)”), a much stronger PRS construction signal (LDpred genome-wide shrinkage with 6.6M variants vs metaGRS with 1.7M), and far broader evaluation with large validation (n=343,676 across multiple ancestries vs n=3,309). Neither record provides PRS-only AUC/R2; PGS000018’s only visible AUROC=0.89 is explicitly a full-model metric (not PRS-comparable) and thus cannot outweigh PGS002244’s stronger structural and validation context. Effect sizes are similar (OR 1.64 vs 1.6), so they do not rescue PGS000018.

PGS004254 is the better-supported Crohn’s disease PRS candidate because it has cleaner endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported is direct “Crohn’s disease” rather than the time-to-event/TTE formulation in PGS001330) and provides strong PRS-relevant effect-size evidence (OR per SD 2.18 [2.05–2.32]), which is a strong discriminator signal even when PRS-only AUC/R² are not reported. In contrast, PGS001330 comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“across 813 traits”) with a very small SNP set (220) and only modest PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.576; PGS-only R² 0.0062), plus a time-to-event endpoint that is a mild mismatch for generic Crohn’s disease risk. While PGS001330 has explicit PRS-only metrics and multi-ancestry evaluation, its framework archetype + sparse construction and weaker discrimination evidence make it less compelling than the disease-focused, genome-wide shrinkage score in PGS004254.

PGS003725 is better supported for generic coronary artery disease risk: it has clean endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported exactly “Coronary artery disease”), strong PRS-discrimination evidence via effect sizes (HR 1.75 and OR 2.14 per SD), and a clearly disease-focused multi-ancestry development/evaluation context with broad external evaluation (EVAL spans AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR/MAE/SAS; validation n=308,264) using only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs). PGS000018 has a slightly less aligned endpoint (“prevalent” CAD) and its only headline discrimination metric is a full-model AUROC=0.89 (not PRS-comparable per the provided policy), with weaker effect-size evidence (OR 1.6) and much smaller listed training sample (n=3,000), so its apparent performance support is less directly attributable to the PRS itself.

Both candidates match the target endpoint well (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported are Crohn’s disease for both), and both use only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs; PGS001331 also includes array type). However, PGS001331 is explicitly a pan-trait UK Biobank framework score (“across 813 traits”) using a very sparse snpnet model (257 variants) with modest PRS-only performance (PGS-only AUROC 0.579, PGS-only R2 0.00677). In contrast, PGS004254 is a disease-focused score using genome-wide shrinkage (LDpred2-auto; 744,682 variants) and reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR 2.18), which is supportive of meaningful PRS discrimination even though it lacks PRS-only AUROC/R2 and only provides a full-model AUROC (0.72) that is not directly comparable. Given the framework penalty and weak PRS-only metrics for PGS001331, the stronger disease-focused/structural evidence and effect-size support favor PGS004254.

Both candidates align to the target trait (dementia) with similar UKB training/validation scale and only basic covariates. However, PGS000929 provides clean PRS-comparable performance (PGS-only AUROC=0.627 and PGS-only R2=0.02346, plus incremental AUROC=0.02294), whereas PGS004284 reports only full-model metrics (AUROC~0.819) with no PGS-only/incremental metric, which the domain guidance says should not be substituted as PRS evidence. PGS000929 also shows broader evaluation ancestry distribution (AFR/EAS/EUR/SAS listed) versus EUR-only for PGS004284, supporting transportability. Despite the framework-paper warning for PGS000929, the lack of PRS-isolated metrics for PGS004284 makes PGS000929 better-supported on the visible fields.

PGS000823 is better supported for the target trait dementia because its phenotyping_reported is an incident dementia endpoint in a disease-focused cohort study context and it provides a PRS-relevant effect size (HR 1.36 top vs bottom tertile) with only basic covariates (age, sex). In contrast, PGS004284 matches the target label exactly (all-cause dementia) and has larger training/validation in UKB, but its only reported discrimination is a full-model AUROC (~0.82) with covariates (age/sex/PCs) and no PGS-only AUC/R2 or effect-size evidence isolating the PRS contribution, making the apparent performance largely non-comparable for PRS ranking. With both lacking PRS-only metrics, the more disease-focused endpoint evidence and PRS-linked HR favors PGS000823.

Both candidates match the target trait well (all-cause dementia; EFO=dementia), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the higher full-model AUROC in PGS004281 (0.819 vs 0.761) is not a reliable differentiator. PGS005170 is better-supported structurally and for transportability: it is an ensemble/integrative PRS (24 component PRSs; 1.32M variants) with multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR) and provides an HR per SD (1.25, 95% CI 1.11–1.42) as PRS-specific evidence. PGS004281 is a very sparse 110-variant single-UKB score evaluated only in EUR, with only covariate-adjusted full-model metrics and no effect-size evidence isolating PRS contribution. Despite PGS005170’s smaller stated training n, its disease-focused integrative design and broader evaluation context make it the stronger choice on the visible fields.

PGS004281 is the better match to the target trait dementia on endpoint fidelity: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported are all explicitly “All-cause dementia/dementia,” whereas PGS000823 is labeled Alzheimer’s disease (trait_efo Alzheimer disease) and only its phenotyping_reported mentions “Incident all-cause dementia,” creating a mixed AD-vs-dementia alignment. Neither candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so PGS004281’s full-model AUROC=0.819 (age/sex/PCs) cannot be treated as PRS performance but is at least a clean, basic-covariate model; PGS000823 provides only a modest HR (top vs bottom tertile 1.36) with no AUC/R2. Although PGS000823 has a multi-cohort disease-focused background, its evaluation is EUR-only and the dementia signal shown is limited; overall the exact dementia endpoint coherence and larger, clearly specified development/validation context in PGS004281 outweigh PGS000823’s AD-centric labeling.

Both candidates are near-clones: same reported trait (MDD lifetime), same EFO mapping, same phenotyping_reported, same method (PRSice-2), same variant count, same training cohort (UKB) and training N, same ancestry distribution and validation N, and both lack PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model R² is shown, which is not a clean PRS-comparable metric). Both candidates are near-clones: same trait_reported/trait_efo (lifetime MDD), same phenotyping_reported, same method (PRSice-2), same training cohort (UKB) and training N (67,164), same covariates (PCs 1-10), same multi-ancestry evaluation mix and validation N (42,250), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R² (only full-model R² is shown, which is not a clean PRS-comparable metric). PGS000823 is better supported for the target trait dementia because it comes from a disease-focused Alzheimer’s/dementia cohort study context with an incident dementia endpoint (phenotyping_reported: incident all-cause dementia) and reports a direct PRS effect size (HR 1.36 top vs bottom tertile) with minimal covariate adjustment (age, sex). Both candidates are near-clones: same reported trait (Major Depressive Disorder, lifetime), same EFO mapping (major depressive disorder), same phenotyping_reported, same method (PRSice-2), same variant count (4,786,322), same training cohort (UKB) and training N (67,164), same covariates (PCs 1–10), same ancestry distribution and validation N (42,250), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R² (only full-model R²). PGS005170 lacks PRS-only AUROC/R2 (only full-model AUROC shown), which lowers confidence, but the endpoint/study archetype and model structure outweigh PGS000929’s modest PRS-only metric advantage.

Both candidates are near-clones: same target endpoint (Major Depressive Disorder lifetime; EFO major depressive disorder), same phenotyping_reported, same method (PRSice-2), same training cohort (UKB) and training N (67,164), same multi-ancestry evaluation mix and validation sample size (42,250), and similarly basic covariates (PCs 1-10). PGS004281 lacks PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC reported, which is not comparable), so confidence is not high, but given the strong framework-penalty signals and very low variant count for PGS000929, PGS004281 is the more credible choice overall.

Both candidates are near-clones: same target endpoint (Major Depressive Disorder lifetime; EFO major depressive disorder; phenotyping_reported major depressive disorder), same method (PRSice-2), same training cohort (UKB) and training N (67,164), same covariates (PCs 1-10), same ancestry distribution and validation size (42,250), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R² (only full-model R² is shown, which is not a clean PRS-comparable metric). Both candidates are near-clones: same endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported = all-cause dementia; trait_efo = dementia), same study/publication/date, same training cohort and size (UKB; n=269,710), same EUR-only dev/eval ancestry, same covariates (age, sex, PC1-10), same validation size (n=67,428), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC/pseudo-R2, which are not PRS-comparable). Both candidates are near-clones: same reported trait (Major Depressive Disorder, lifetime), same EFO mapping, same phenotyping_reported, same method (PRSice-2), same training cohort (UKB) and training N (67,164), same covariates (PCs 1-10), same multi-ancestry evaluation mix and validation N (42,250), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R² (only full-model R² is shown, which is not a clean PRS-comparable metric). Both candidates are near-clones: same endpoint fidelity (Major Depressive Disorder lifetime; EFO major depressive disorder; phenotyping_reported MDD), same method (PRSice-2), same training cohort (UKB) and training N (67,164), same covariates (PCs 1-10), same evaluation ancestry mix and validation N (42,250), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R² (only full-model R²). Both candidates are near-clones: same reported trait (Major Depressive Disorder (Lifetime)), same EFO (major depressive disorder), same phenotyping_reported (Major depressive disorder), same method (PRSice-2), same training cohort (UKB) and training N (67,164), same covariates (PCs 1-10), same multi-ancestry evaluation mix and validation sample size (42,250), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R² (only full-model R² is shown, which is not a clean PRS-comparable metric). PGS005170 is the better-supported match to the target trait dementia because its reported trait and EFO mapping align directly to dementia ("All-cause dementia"; trait_efo="dementia") with the same incident all-cause dementia phenotyping as PGS000823, but it is built as a modern integrative/ensemble PRS (24 component PRSs; 1,320,229 variants) and shows multi-ancestry evaluation coverage (AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR) plus a per-SD HR (1.25) alongside a reported AUROC (0.761) albeit as a full-model metric. Both candidates are near-clones: same reported trait (Major Depressive Disorder, lifetime), same EFO mapping (major depressive disorder), same phenotyping_reported (Major depressive disorder), same method (PRSice-2), same training cohort (UKB) and training N (67,164), same covariates (PCs 1-10), same validation N (42,250), and identical multi-ancestry evaluation distribution. Both candidates target the same trait concept (Dilated cardiomyopathy (MTAG), EFO dilated cardiomyopathy) and use the same method (PRS-CS) with broadly comparable, non-leaky covariates (basic sex/PC adjustment; PGS004862 also includes age/age^2). However, PGS004951 provides more PRS-attributable performance evidence via explicit delta PRS/residual R² metrics and a stated univariate (PRS-only) AUC=0.67 (with CI), whereas PGS004862 reports only full-model AUROC=0.71/R²=0.05 without isolating PRS contribution. PGS004951 is better supported for dilated cardiomyopathy because it provides PRS-comparable performance evidence (explicit univariate PRS-only AUC=0.67 with CI and delta PRS/residual liability-scale R²=0.101), whereas PGS004861 reports only full-model AUROC/R² (0.70/0.048) without isolating PRS contribution. Endpoint fidelity is acceptable for both (both map to dilated cardiomyopathy; PGS004951’s phenotyping is explicitly clinical DCM and MTAG is not a negative). Although PGS004861 has a much larger EUR validation sample (n=347,585 vs n=7,761) and slightly cleaner/basic covariates, PGS004951’s stronger effect size (OR 1.93 vs 1.56) plus explicit PRS-only metrics outweigh the validation-size advantage, and its PRS-only R² remains below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.17), supporting plausibility.

Both candidates are near-clones: same target-aligned endpoint (Major Depressive Disorder, lifetime; EFO major depressive disorder), same phenotyping_reported, same method (PRSice-2), same training cohort (UKB) and training N (67,164), same covariates (PCs 1-10), same multi-ancestry evaluation mix and validation N (42,250), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R² (only full-model R² is shown, which is not a clean PRS-comparable metric). With endpoint and design essentially identical, the only differentiators are small full-model R² and variant count; PGS003580 has slightly higher reported R² (0.0254 vs 0.0207), while PGS003584 has more variants. Given the guidance that small full-model metric differences are weak but still the only performance signal available here, PGS003580 edges out PGS003584, though the evidence gap is minimal.

PGS004862 is preferred because it is the MTAG-enhanced version of the same dilated cardiomyopathy endpoint (trait_reported: "Dilated cardiomyopathy (MTAG)" vs PGS004861 "Dilated cardiomyopathy"), and domain guidance explicitly mildly prefers MTAG variants within the same study family as a power-boost rather than an endpoint mismatch. Both candidates otherwise match the target trait equally well (same trait_efo and phenotyping_reported), come from the same Nat Genet paper, use the same method (PRS-CS), same EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, same covariates, same training cohort label (HERMES), and same validation N. With no PRS-only AUC/R2 for either, the small full-model AUROC/R2 differences are weak but still slightly favor PGS004862 (AUROC 0.71 vs 0.70; R² 0.05 vs 0.048) and it also shows a stronger per-SD OR (1.76 vs 1.56).

Both candidates target dilated cardiomyopathy with the same reported trait label “Dilated cardiomyopathy (MTAG)” and similar basic covariates (age/age^2/sex/PCs) using the same method (PRS-CS), so endpoint/method differences are limited. PGS004947 has more informative PRS-specific performance evidence: it explicitly reports a univariate (PRS-only) AUC=0.66 (with CI) and delta R² metrics attributable to PRS, whereas PGS004862 reports only full-model AUROC=0.71 and R²=0.05 without PRS-only/incremental decomposition, making its discrimination less comparable for PRS quality. Although PGS004862 has a larger EUR evaluation sample (n=347,585 vs n=96,016) and a slightly more generic phenotype label (“Dilated cardiomyopathy” vs “Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy”), PGS004947’s phenotype remains closely aligned and its PRS-isolated metrics provide stronger direct support for standalone PRS performance.

PGS004947 is better supported for dilated cardiomyopathy because it provides PRS-comparable performance evidence (explicit univariate PRS-only AUC=0.66 with CI and delta PRS/residual R² metrics) and a stronger per-SD effect size (OR=1.73) than PGS004861 (only full-model AUROC=0.70 and full-model R²=0.048 with no PRS-only metrics; OR=1.56). Endpoint alignment is acceptable for both (both map to dilated cardiomyopathy; PGS004947’s phenotyping is non-ischemic DCM and labeled MTAG, which is not a negative per the provided guidance). Although PGS004861 has a larger EUR evaluation sample (n=347,585 vs n=96,016) and cleaner EUR-only evaluation ancestry, validation size is a weak tie-breaker and does not outweigh PGS004947’s clearer PRS-only metric reporting and stronger effect-size evidence.

Both candidates are near-clones from the same Nat Genet study (PRS-CS, ~1.0M variants, same trait_reported/trait_efo) and both report similar PRS-only AUROC (PGS004951: 0.67 [0.65–0.69] vs PGS004949: 0.68 [0.66–0.69]) and similar per-SD OR (~1.9). The key differentiator is endpoint fidelity and evaluation coherence for the target ‘dilated cardiomyopathy’: PGS004951 uses ‘Clinical dilated cardiomyopathy’ and is evaluated in EUR (100%), matching the trait directly, whereas PGS004949 is explicitly ‘Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy’ (a subtype) and is evaluated in MAE (100%) with a confusing selected_validation_ancestry field (‘European, Not reported’), reducing clarity/compatibility. Although PGS004949 has a slightly higher PRS-only AUROC and much larger validation N, those advantages are weak/tie-break signals here and don’t outweigh the cleaner direct-DCM endpoint and ancestry alignment of PGS004951.

PGS004614 is better supported for the target trait because it is clearly disease-focused on diverticular disease (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both “Diverticular disease”) and shows broader evaluation ancestry (AFR/EUR/SAS) rather than EUR-only, which is supportive of transportability. Although its only reported discrimination is a full-model AUROC=0.76 (not PRS-only and likely influenced by covariates including family history), PGS004474 provides even less directly comparable performance evidence (no AUC/R2; only a modest OR per SD ~1.31) and comes from a “risk factor PRS + disease PRS integration” framing that raises packaging/augmentation concerns with unknown covariates. Overall, PGS004614 has the cleaner endpoint framing and more robust evaluation context, while PGS004474 lacks comparable metrics and has more risk-wrapper signals.

Both candidates are near-clones for the target trait (same trait_efo dilated cardiomyopathy; same reported MTAG framing; same phenotyping_reported non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy; same method PRS-CS; similar ~1.0M variant counts) and neither provides top-level PRS-only AUC/R2, so the decision rests on the PRS-isolated metrics/effect sizes and comparability. PGS004949 shows consistently stronger PRS signal than PGS004947: higher univariate (PRS-only) AUC (0.68 vs 0.66) with tighter CI, higher per-SD OR (1.91 vs 1.73) and beta (0.65 vs 0.55), and higher liability-scale delta R2 (0.095 vs 0.076). Covariates are both basic; although PGS004949 includes array adjustment (not a leakage concern), PGS004947’s slightly cleaner covariate list and slightly higher full-model R2 do not outweigh the stronger PRS-only/effect-size evidence and much larger validation sample in PGS004949 (326,106 vs 96,016).

PGS000997 is better supported for the target trait (diverticular disease) because it maps cleanly to the same EFO trait and uses a direct diagnosis endpoint (“Diverticular disease of intestine”), whereas PGS000996 broadens the endpoint to a mixed concept (“diverticular disease, diverticulitis”), adding phenotype ambiguity relative to the target. Both are from the same pan-trait UKB snpnet framework paper with identical training cohort (UKB), covariates (age/sex/array/PCs), and similar multi-ancestry evaluation structure, so performance evidence becomes the main differentiator: PGS000997 has materially stronger PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.591 vs 0.552; PGS-only R² 0.0178 vs 0.0037) and higher incremental AUROC (0.0173 vs 0.0084). Validation N is larger for PGS000996, but per the guidance this is a weak tie-break and does not outweigh the clearer endpoint alignment plus stronger PRS-only performance of PGS000997.

Both candidates have strong endpoint fidelity to dupuytren contracture (matching trait_efo and consistent phenotyping_reported). However, PGS001254 comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“across 813 traits”, snpnet) with an extremely small variant set (11), which is a known warning pattern for generalizability despite reporting clean PRS-only AUROC/R² (0.6646 / 0.0247). PGS002092, while lacking PRS-only AUROC/R², is a genome-wide shrinkage score (LDpred2) with very large variant coverage (~484k) and is explicitly evaluated across multiple ancestries (AFR/EUR/GME/SAS), providing stronger transportability evidence than EUR-only evaluation in PGS001254. Given the framework+sparsity concerns for PGS001254 and the stronger structural/portability support for PGS002092, PGS002092 is better-supported overall.

PGS000997 has cleaner, directly comparable PRS-only performance reported for diverticular disease (PGS-only AUROC=0.591 and PGS-only R²=0.0178 with basic covariates listed), allowing a sanity check against the trait’s heritability ceiling and avoiding reliance on full-model metrics. It also shows broader evaluation ancestry coverage (EUR plus AFR/EAS/SAS in eval), which is supportive for transportability. In contrast, PGS004474 has an endpoint-aligned ICD10 K57 phenotype and a genome-wide LDpred2 build with an OR≈1.31, but it lacks PRS-comparable AUC/R² entirely and has unknown covariates, making its predictive strength and comparability harder to judge from the visible fields. Despite PGS000997 coming from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (a negative archetype signal), the absence of comparable metrics for PGS004474 leaves PGS000997 better-supported overall on-record.

PGS004614 is the better-supported diverticular disease PRS because it comes from a disease-focused diverticular-disease GWAS paper and shows broader evaluation ancestry (AFR/EUR/SAS) rather than EUR-only, supporting transportability. Although its only reported discrimination is a full-model AUROC=0.76 (not PRS-only) and it includes family history (covariate leakage concern), PGS004544 provides even less directly comparable performance evidence (no AUC/R2; only a modest OR=1.32) and comes from a risk-factor integration/metaPRS framework-style study with unknown covariates, making it harder to interpret as a standalone disease PRS. Endpoint fidelity is acceptable for both (K57 ICD10 vs generic diverticular disease), so the decision rests on study archetype/validation context and the stronger disease-specific evidence package favoring PGS004614.

Both candidates target dilated cardiomyopathy with the same reported trait label “Dilated cardiomyopathy (MTAG)” and similar basic covariates (age/sex/PCs; no obvious clinical-risk packaging). However, PGS004949 provides cleaner PRS-attributable performance evidence: it explicitly reports a univariate (PRS-only) AUC of 0.68 (with CI) and delta R² metrics (e.g., liability-scale delta PRS/residual R²=0.095), whereas PGS004862 reports only full-model AUROC=0.71 and R²=0.05 without PRS-only/incremental decomposition, making its discrimination less comparable for PRS quality. PGS004949 also shows a slightly stronger effect size (OR 1.91 vs 1.76) and a substantially larger variant count within the same method (PRS-CS; 1,038,394 vs 709,534). The main drawback for PGS004949 is endpoint/evaluation mismatch (phenotyping_reported is non-ischemic DCM and evaluation is MAE-only), but given the stronger PRS-isolated metrics and effect size, it is better-supported overall than PGS004862.

PGS002304 is the cleaner endpoint match to the target: both trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are explicitly “Follicular lymphoma,” whereas PGS000644 is labeled/phenotyped as “Nodular lymphoma” despite mapping to the same EFO, creating endpoint-fidelity ambiguity. Neither record provides PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC values are not strong cross-model PRS evidence; the small AUROC difference (0.61 vs 0.538) is not decisive, especially with different/unknown covariates (PGS002304 covariates unknown; PGS000644 includes age/sex/PCs/batch). Although PGS000644 has a much more polygenic construction (lassosum, ~2.2M variants) and larger validation n, the domain guidance prioritizes phenotype alignment over structural signals when PRS-only metrics are absent, so the exact follicular-lymphoma endpoint coherence in PGS002304 makes it better supported overall.

PGS000997 is better supported on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports clean PGS-only AUROC (0.591) and PGS-only R² (0.0178) with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array), and the PRS-only R² is plausible relative to the provided diverticular-disease heritability ceiling. It also has larger, clearly stated training (n=269,704) and broader multi-ancestry evaluation. PGS004614 is disease-focused and uses a stronger genome-wide shrinkage method with many variants, but its only visible discrimination is a full-model AUROC (0.76) with family history included and no PGS-only metrics, making its performance less comparable and potentially covariate-inflated; training sample size is also missing. Overall, the direct PRS-only metric support in PGS000997 outweighs the structural advantages of PGS004614 given the missing/packaged performance evidence.

PGS000997 is better supported on comparable PRS evidence: it reports clean PRS-only AUROC/R² (PGS-only AUROC=0.591, PGS-only R²=0.0178) with basic covariates listed and a multi-ancestry evaluation set, and its PRS-only R² is in a plausible range relative to the diverticular disease heritability ceiling. In contrast, PGS004544 has an endpoint-aligned ICD10 K57 phenotype and a moderate per-SD OR (1.32) plus many variants, but it provides no PRS-comparable AUC/R² at all and has unknown covariates, making its predictive performance and comparability much less evidenced in the visible fields. Despite PGS000997 coming from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (a negative archetype signal), the absence of usable discrimination metrics for PGS004544 leaves PGS000997 as the more empirically supported choice here.

PGS002304 has coherent endpoint fidelity for the target trait: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to follicular lymphoma, whereas PGS003455 has an explicit phenotyping_reported mismatch ("Chronic lymphocytic leukemia") despite follicular lymphoma labels, which is a major red flag given phenotyping_reported is the primary endpoint field. Neither candidate provides PRS-only AUC/R2, so PGS002304’s reported full-model AUROC=0.61 cannot be treated as PRS performance but still offers some validation signal, while PGS003455 provides only a weak per-SD OR=1.07 with CI crossing 1.0. Although PGS003455 has a much larger validation sample size and slightly more variants (7 vs 6), validation size is a weak tie-break and does not outweigh the endpoint incoherence and weaker effect-size evidence.

Both candidates are endpoint-identical for the target (same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported), come from the same UKB portability paper, have the same training size, covariates, ancestry distribution, and no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported—so performance evidence is essentially tied. The main differentiators are structural: PGS002092 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far broader variant coverage (484,484 vs 2,443 for PGS001880), and it has a slightly higher partial correlation in the selected record (0.0797 vs 0.0783). Given the lack of cleaner PRS-only metrics, the method/coverage advantage makes PGS002092 better-supported.

Both candidates are essentially near-clones for diverticular disease (same ICD10 K57 endpoint in trait_reported/phenotyping_reported, same EFO mapping, same publication, same EUR-only training/evaluation, same variant count, same training and validation sample sizes) and neither reports PRS-comparable AUC/R2, so performance evidence is limited to per-SD OR. PGS004544 has a slightly higher reported OR (1.321 vs 1.312 for PGS004474), and its method (RFDiseasemetaPRS) suggests multi-score/meta-PRS aggregation, which is a mild positive structural signal over a single-score LDpred2 when other fields are indistinguishable. The advantage is small, hence low confidence.

PGS004544 is the better-supported choice for diverticular disease because it has tighter endpoint fidelity to the target ICD10 diagnosis (phenotyping_reported/trait_reported: K57 diverticular disease of intestine; trait_efo: diverticular disease) and comes from a disease-focused integration/meta-PRS archetype (RFDiseasemetaPRS) with genome-wide coverage (1,059,939 variants) and a moderate per-SD effect size (OR≈1.32). In contrast, PGS000996 is a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse framework score (“across 813 traits”) with very low PRS-only performance (PGS-only AUROC≈0.552; R2≈0.0037) and only 368 variants—signals consistent with weak standalone PRS utility despite having clean PRS-only metrics and broader evaluation ancestries. Given the framework-penalty and weak PRS-only metrics for PGS000996, PGS004544’s disease-aligned endpoint and stronger structural design outweigh its missing PRS-only AUC/R2.

Both candidates target primary open-angle glaucoma, but PGS001792 provides a clean PRS-comparable metric (PGS-only / covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.03209) whereas PGS004944 reports only a full-model AUROC (0.748) that is not comparable as a standalone PRS metric. PGS001792’s PRS-only R2 is also plausible under the glaucoma heritability ceiling guidance, and it comes from a multi-biobank portability/lessons study with explicit training cohorts and basic covariates (age/sex/PCs). PGS004944 has supportive OR per SD (1.74) and broader listed validation ancestries, but its endpoint is self-reported POAG and the lack of PRS-only AUC/R2 makes its performance evidence less directly supported than PGS001792 in this head-to-head.

PGS000644 is the better-supported PRS for follicular lymphoma because its endpoint fields are coherent with the target (trait_efo=follicular lymphoma and phenotyping_reported/trait_reported use the near-synonymous ICD-style wording “Nodular lymphoma”), and it provides a clear evaluation package (European eval, basic covariates age/sex/PCs/batch, and reported discrimination/effect sizes including full-model AUROC=0.538 and OR per SD=1.149). In contrast, PGS003455 has a critical endpoint-fidelity problem: despite trait_reported=Follicular lymphoma and trait_efo=follicular lymphoma, its phenotyping_reported is “Chronic lymphocytic leukemia,” indicating likely phenotype/metadata mismatch; it also lacks training details and any AUC/R2 metrics, with only a weak OR=1.07. Given phenotype alignment is the top criterion, PGS000644 wins.

PGS004474 is the better-supported choice for the target diverticular disease because its endpoint fidelity is tighter (ICD10 K57 diverticular disease of intestine in both trait_reported and phenotyping_reported, mapped to diverticular disease) and it comes from a disease-focused study context using a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very large variant coverage (~1.06M), which is structurally favored over sparse pan-trait UKB framework scores. Although PGS000996 reports clean PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC 0.5519; PGS R2 0.00372) and has multi-ancestry evaluation, it is explicitly from the ‘813 traits’ sparse snpnet framework with only 368 variants and shows weak PRS signal; its broader phenotype label (diverticular disease/diverticulitis) is slightly less specific to the target. PGS004474 lacks PRS-only AUC/R2, but it at least provides an OR per SD (~1.31, moderate signal) and avoids the framework/sparse-model penalty that dominates against PGS000996 here.

PGS002304 is the cleaner endpoint match for the target trait: trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are both explicitly “Follicular lymphoma,” whereas PGS000643 is labeled “Nodular lymphoma” in both trait_reported and phenotyping_reported (despite mapping to the same EFO), creating avoidable endpoint-fidelity ambiguity. Neither candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC values are not strong cross-model PRS evidence; still, PGS002304’s reported AUROC (0.61) is higher than PGS000643’s (0.532) without any explicit heavy covariate packaging in either record (PGS000643 uses basic age/sex/PCs; PGS002304 covariates are unknown). Although PGS000643 has stronger methodological/structural signals (PRS-CS with ~1.0M variants and larger validation n=3,256 vs 6 SNPs and n=197), the primary criterion here is phenotype alignment, and PGS002304 is the more directly faithful follicular lymphoma record.

Both candidates are endpoint-faithful to dupuytren contracture (same trait_efo; phenotyping_reported is a direct Dupuytren/palmar fascia contracture diagnosis in both). PGS001254 has clean PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC 0.6646; PGS R2 0.0247) but comes from the pan-trait UKB “813 traits” sparse snpnet framework with only 11 variants and EUR-only evaluation, a study archetype that domain guidance flags as less reliable for external generalization. PGS001880, while lacking PRS-only AUROC/R2, is a denser penalized-regression score (2443 variants) from the UKB portability study and is evaluated across multiple ancestries (AFR/EUR/GME/SAS), providing stronger visible transportability evidence and a PRS-comparable signal (partial-r 0.0783). Given similar phenotype alignment, the broader multi-ancestry evaluation and less extremely sparse architecture make PGS001880 better-supported overall despite missing AUROC/R2.

PGS004949 is better supported for dilated cardiomyopathy because it provides PRS-comparable performance evidence (explicit univariate PRS-only AUC=0.68 with CI and delta R² metrics) and a stronger reported effect size (OR=1.91) than PGS004861 (OR=1.56), which only reports full-model AUROC/R² without isolating PRS contribution. Endpoint alignment is acceptable for both (both map to dilated cardiomyopathy; PGS004949’s phenotyping is non-ischemic DCM, a close clinical subtype), and covariates are similarly basic, so the presence of PRS-only metrics and stronger effect size in PGS004949 outweigh PGS004861’s slightly higher full-model AUROC and EUR-only evaluation.

PGS000643 is the better-supported follicular lymphoma PRS despite imperfect labeling: its trait_efo matches follicular lymphoma and its reported phenotype (“Nodular lymphoma”) is a near-synonym/ICD10-aligned concept for follicular [nodular] lymphoma, whereas PGS003455 has a direct trait_reported match but an explicit phenotyping mismatch (“Chronic lymphocytic leukemia”), which is a different disease and a major endpoint-fidelity red flag. Neither candidate provides PRS-only AUC/R2; PGS000643 at least reports evaluation metrics (full-model AUROC 0.532 with basic covariates and OR top 1% vs rest 2.49) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS, ~1.0M variants), while PGS003455 is a 7-SNP GWAS-hits score with only a weak per-SD OR (~1.07) and unknown covariates. Overall, PGS000643 has more coherent endpoint alignment and stronger structural/effect-size support than PGS003455.

Both candidates are near-clones for the target (trait_efo=follicular lymphoma; phenotyping_reported/trait_reported=Nodular lymphoma), from the same publication/cohort context (MGI; EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL; same training n=3,696 and validation n=3,256; same basic covariates). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we cannot use clean PRS-comparable metrics; the small full-model AUROC difference is likely noise. As a tie-break, PGS000644 shows slightly stronger overall discrimination signals (higher full-model AUROC 0.538 vs 0.532, higher pseudo-R² 0.00349 vs 0.00282, and slightly higher per-SD OR 1.149 vs 1.133), while PGS000643’s only standout is OR top 1% vs rest. Given the otherwise identical design, PGS000644 is marginally better supported, but the edge is small (low confidence).

PGS004614 is the better-supported choice for the target trait (diverticular disease) because it is disease-focused with exact endpoint alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Diverticular disease”) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (SBayesR) with very large genome-wide coverage (1,082,282 variants), plus multi-ancestry evaluation is indicated. Although its only visible discrimination is a full-model AUROC=0.76 (not PRS-only) and it includes family history as a covariate (making that AUROC potentially covariate-inflated), the competing PGS000996 is a pan-trait UK Biobank “813 traits” sparse snpnet score (framework archetype) with a very weak PRS-only signal (PGS-only AUROC=0.5519; PGS-only R2=0.00372) and a slightly broader/less specific endpoint (“Diverticular disease/diverticulitis”). Given the strong framework penalty and low PRS-only performance for PGS000996, PGS004614’s disease-specific study context and stronger structural properties outweigh the metric-availability advantage of PGS000996.

Both candidates target the same endpoint (phenotyping_reported/trait_reported = Primary open-angle glaucoma) with the same method (PRS-CS-auto) and very similar PRS-only Nagelkerke R2 (PGS001792: 0.03209 vs PGS001797: 0.031479), both well below the glaucoma heritability ceiling provided. With endpoint fidelity essentially tied, PGS001792 has a slight edge on PRS-comparable performance (higher covariates-regressed-out R2) and a much larger reported validation sample size (347,396 vs 7,128), while PGS001797’s broader training cohort list does not clearly outweigh those advantages given the near-clone nature of the records. Differences in full-model AUROC (0.777 vs 0.749) are secondary and not decisive. Overall this is a near-tie, hence low confidence, but PGS001792 is marginally better supported.

PGS004951 is better supported for the target trait (dilated cardiomyopathy) because its endpoint is the direct clinical DCM phenotype (phenotyping_reported: "Clinical dilated cardiomyopathy"), whereas PGS004947 targets a narrower subtype ("Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy"), which is a mild endpoint-fidelity mismatch for a generic DCM target. On PRS-comparable evidence, both report similar PRS-only AUCs, but PGS004951 is slightly higher (0.67 vs 0.66) and shows stronger PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.93 vs 1.73) and larger delta PRS/residual liability-scale R² (0.101 vs 0.076), supporting a stronger standalone PRS contribution. Although PGS004947 has a much larger validation sample and a higher full-model liability R², those are weaker tie-break signals and the full-model metric is less comparable given heavier covariates (includes age and age^2 vs sex+PCs only in PGS004951).

PGS001792 is better supported for glaucoma because it provides a clean PRS-comparable performance metric (PGS-only / covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.03209) in a very large European validation (n=347,396), with endpoint fidelity to the target via a specific clinical subtype (primary open-angle glaucoma) mapped to glaucoma. Its PRS-only R2 is also plausible relative to the provided glaucoma heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.0556). In contrast, PGS002761 has a broader glaucoma label but reports no PRS-comparable AUC/R2 at all (only an OR=1.68) and has much smaller validation (n=39,444) with EUR-only GWAS/EVAL, giving less directly comparable and less robust evidence on the visible fields.

PGS001792 is better supported for glaucoma PRS quality because it provides a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke’s R2 with covariates regressed out / pgs_only_r2=0.03209) with basic demographic/PC covariates, and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS-auto) with very large variant coverage (911,402), which is structurally favorable for a polygenic disease. Its PRS-only R2 is also plausible relative to the provided glaucoma heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.0556), suggesting the metric is not obviously inflated. In contrast, PGS000137 is disease-focused and endpoint-aligned (phenotyping_reported POAG) but reports only a full-model AUROC (0.8) and includes self-reported family history as a covariate, making its discrimination less PRS-comparable; it also uses a much sparser C+T score (2,673 variants) with limited standalone PRS performance evidence.

PGS004944 is more endpoint-faithful to the target glaucoma context by focusing on primary open-angle glaucoma (trait_efo open-angle glaucoma) with explicit phenotyping as POAG (self-reported) and shows broader transportability evidence via multi-ancestry GWAS (AFR/EAS/EUR) and multi-ancestry validation coverage (selected_validation_ancestry spans African, Hispanic/LatAm, East/South Asian, European) with a very large validation sample (n=407,667). Although its only AUROC is a full-model AUROC=0.748 (not PRS-only), its covariates are basic (age/age^2/sex/ancestry) and it reports a strong per-SD OR=1.74. In contrast, PGS002761 has a broader but less specific endpoint label (“Glaucoma”) and comes from a cross-disease comparison framework paper (“across 24 common diseases”), with EUR-only GWAS/EVAL and much smaller validation (n=39,444); it provides no AUROC/R2 metrics and only a slightly weaker OR=1.68. With neither candidate offering PRS-only AUC/R2, the stronger endpoint specificity plus broader validation context favors PGS004944.

PGS004944 is better supported for the target trait glaucoma because its endpoint is explicitly primary open-angle glaucoma (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported), which is a clinically central glaucoma subtype and aligns well with the target, and it shows stronger PRS signal evidence via an OR per SD of 1.74. It is also evaluated at very large scale (n=407,667) and across multiple ancestries in the selected validation context, supporting transportability. PGS000137 has a slightly higher reported AUROC (0.8 vs 0.748), but both candidates only provide full-model AUROC (no PGS-only AUC/R2), and PGS000137’s covariates include family history, which is a clinical augmentation that makes the AUROC less comparable to standalone PRS performance; it also lacks effect-size evidence. Given the lack of PRS-only metrics in both, the cleaner covariate set and stronger effect-size evidence favor PGS004944.

Both candidates are near-clones for the target trait gout: identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (Gout), same publication, same training cohort (UKB) and training N (6,704), same evaluation ancestry mix (EUR/SAS) and validation N (90,274), and both list covariates as 0 with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported (so full-model AUROC/R² are only weakly informative). Given this near-tie, PGS004047 is better-supported on the visible performance/effect-size fields: it has slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.685 vs 0.678), higher R² (0.0801 vs 0.0734), and stronger per-SD effect sizes (OR 1.999 vs 1.927; β 0.693 vs 0.656) than PGS004018, making it the stronger sibling within the same endpoint family.

PGS001797 is better supported for the target trait because it has tighter endpoint fidelity to glaucoma as a clinically dominant subtype (primary open-angle glaucoma; EFO open-angle glaucoma) and, crucially, reports a PRS-comparable performance metric (PGS-only / covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.031479) that is interpretable as PRS signal, whereas PGS002761 provides no PRS-only AUC/R2 at all (only an OR per SD=1.68). Although PGS002761 matches the umbrella label “glaucoma” and has a larger EUR validation sample (n=39,444 vs n=7,128), validation size is a weak tie-break and does not compensate for missing comparable discrimination metrics. Both use only basic covariates and EUR evaluation, but PGS001797 also has clearer multi-cohort development context listed, adding support beyond the single effect-size-only evidence in PGS002761.

Both candidates are essentially endpoint-identical for the target trait (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all = gout), come from the same publication, have the same training cohort (UKB), training N (n=6,704), ancestry distribution (DEV EUR; EVAL EUR/SAS), covariates=0, and the same validation sample size (n=90,274), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (so full-model AUROC is only a weak within-family signal).
